newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MIM says near world's best practice.
newsitem.headline: MIM says near world's best practice.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd's chief executive Nick Stump said on Friday that new labour agreements at the giant Mt Isa base metals mine in Queensland will allow the mines to become one of best mining operations in the world.

"We have a very firm belief operational change must come from within," Stump told a meeting of the Securities Institute of Australia. "Mt Isa will return to be one of the best mines in the world," he said. "We're confident world's best practice will be in our operations by the year 2000."
"In the last few months, enterprise bargaining agreements have been established over three major areas - mining metallugical and services," Stump said.
"These agreements cover the entire workforce with work and pay agreements relevant to these three areas," he said.
Stump said MIM was well on its way to achieving a single-status work force at Mt Isa.
"Now, our competitive disadvantage has practically been eliminated," he said.
Stump described Mt Isa's changes in labour relations as "remarkable", with the majority of employees wanting world's best practice conditions.
Pay incentives had moved to being based on individual performance rather than piece-work arrangements, he said.
"We now have 'hot seat' shift changes at our underground operations. We used to lose 1-1/2 hours every day on shift changes," Stump said.
However, he said there are still tough times ahead for mining companies "unless metal prices or exchange rates improve."
"We'll be a medium-sized mining company. It is a new era for MIM," Stump said.

Stump also said there was no reason why the Ernest Henry copper-gold mining project in north-west Queensland could not proceed, despite a native title claim being lodged over the mine area by the Mitakoodi Juhnjlar Aboriginal Corporation.
"There should be no reason why (Ernest Henry) should be delayed," Stump said.

Stump said Ernest Henry's mining lease was granted in 1974 with the 1993 Native Title Act excluding all mining leases prior to 1975. "We have threats on the mine's infrastructure but the mine itself is not under threat," he said.
"What we're seeing is an attempt to raise the stakes everywhere," Stump said.
Ernest Henry production is scheduled to start in the second half of 1997 at an annual rate of 350,000 tonnes containing 95,000 tonnes of copper and 120,000 ounces of gold.
